goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: Required commands pass and declaration hashes match, but the drift contract does not authenticate runtime facts. Both recorded runtime-source SHA-256 values are wrong; the helper never reads those sources and only compares the manifest with a duplicated runtimeContract in provenance. It also omits exact FlowConfig, presentation, issue, condition, transition-branch, registration, and required/optional property contracts, plus immediate-default and custom-easing defaults. Source or option drift can therefore pass while documentation becomes stale. Replace the proxy contract with authenticated runtime snapshots and source-derived parity before documentation depends on it.
evidence: Fresh focused verification passed: 24 Vitest tests, focused ESLint, production build, and git diff --check.
Exact-commit raw declaration snapshots match recorded SHA-256 and Git blob SHAs.

Exact-commit screen-transition-config.ts hashes to SHA-256 c50100c0cc713c947c8d5e617d32fca4ec17bf9ff565887391e9a157486614f8, not recorded 786cb0a16405329a92f3f79b3b76a8f71109ecd72b0276ddbe4ee38f06c0babd.
Exact-commit screen-transition.ts hashes to SHA-256 b74a94dcfc1913c0d1e5f83603ac49376a5ad9238facaf63d9d0d74be66272a1, not recorded 9fbfbd0a8c81544460ba8aeff0f408a1a1b541dcc78dc6b94e83f8512bf0a06a.

test/helpers/flow-capability-parity.ts reads only declarations and provenance; runtimeSources are neither typed, read, hashed, nor parsed. Lines 295-305 merely deep-compare two hand-maintained runtimeContract copies.

The parity helper queries selected FlowConfig members but never exact-compares FlowConfig, presentation, or issue property sets; presentation.screenTransition and BugDropPublicAPI.registerFlow are absent from the manifest.

Condition coverage extracts only each branch's first member, so equals/recursive-array shape drift is undetected. Transition coverage extracts kinds/easing but not exact branch properties or requiredness.

The released implementation proves omitted/none transitions and first render replace immediately, while custom easing defaults to standard; neither default is represented or source-derived in the manifest.
